sources: https://winterwi.com/about-the-winter-wisconsin-area/area-attractions/the-ojibwa-park/ (Winter Area Chamber of Commerce's page for the Town of Ojibwa's park - the town has no website of its own; read live with the headless browser, desktop Chrome UA, 2026-11-20; the stored http://www.winterwi.com/the-ojibwa-park/ redirects here): 'The Board of The Town of Ojibwa Welcomes You to Ojibwa Park. Opens May 1st and closes October 30th each year.'; 'Wisconsin Highway 70 bisects Ojibwa Park between Ojibwa and Winter'; 'The Park consists of a camping area with 16 camper sites, 3 tent sites, several picnic areas and a small stream and pond. An RV dump station, drinking water and pit toilets are available.'; 'There is a trail connecting the parking area with the Tuscobia State Trail, which is a popular ATV, snowmobile and mountain bike trail.'; 'The park is open for camping from the first of May to the last day of the regular gun deer hunting season (near the end of November). The campsites in the Park are available on a first come/ first serve basis. Each of the three non-electric sites has a nightly fee. Each of the twelve electric sites has a nightly fee. Coin operated showers were added in 2016.'; contact 'Ojibwa Park Committee Chair (715) 945-2652'.

https://winterwi.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/ojibwa_park_map_large.jpg (park map linked from that page, uploaded 2025-05): campground loop south of Hwy 70 with 'Camper Sites (16)' and 'Tent Sites (3)'; the Chippewa River and a canoe landing are north of the highway; 'East ATV Access to Tuscobia Trail' leaves the campground loop south, 'West ATV Access' and a loading ramp at the main park lot.

Esri World Imagery (tools/sat.py, 2026-11-20) around 45.8059,-91.0881: the campground loop centres ~45.8054,-91.0856, ~200 m ESE of the pin, in woods south of Hwy 70; the Chippewa River lies ~120 m+ north across the highway.
Aggregators (corroboration only, not used for values): The Dyrt lists three non-electric sites $15 and twelve electric $20 and a Dec 1 - Apr 30 closure (2024-25); RV Life $20 (Sep 2022).

note: Town of Ojibwa park on Hwy 70 between Ojibwa and Winter: a wooded camping loop south of the highway, with the Chippewa River (canoe landing) across the road and nature and ski trails. Electric and non-electric sites; coin showers. A trail from the campground reaches the Tuscobia State Trail (ATV, snowmobile, bike). --Claude
summary: Chamber page (the town's park listing) now loads in the headless browser: FCFS only, coin showers since 2016, dump, water, pit toilets; 12 electric + 3 non-electric camper sites (vs '16 camper sites'); season stated two ways; no official rate. Not waterfront confirmed; pin OK.
flags: FEES: no official rate anywhere - the page says only that each site 'has a nightly fee'. The Dyrt ($15 non-electric / $20 electric, 2024-25) and RV Life ($20, 2022) are aggregator-only, so fees stay unset. A call to the park committee chair (715) 945-2652 would price it.

SEASON: the page says both 'Opens May 1st and closes October 30th each year' and 'open for camping from the first of May to the last day of the regular gun deer hunting season (near the end of November)'. Left unset; if one is wanted, the header line gives 05-01..10-30.
SITES: '16 camper sites, 3 tent sites' (map agrees) vs 'three non-electric sites ... twelve electric sites' later on the same page. Stored count 19 kept; electric amperage not stated.

OHV: a general town park campground with ATV access - the map shows an 'East ATV Access to Tuscobia Trail' leaving the campground loop and an ATV loading ramp at the main lot; the park itself is picnic/nature/river-oriented. Per the rule (general campground with an ATV side stays) - flagged for the reviewer, not a drop.
WATERFRONT: not waterfront confirmed (sweep value, no --AWH): Hwy 70 lies between the campground and the Chippewa River.
PIN: stored 45.8059,-91.0881 is at the park entrance on Hwy 70, ~200 m from the loop (~45.8054,-91.0856) - under 250 m, no move.
